chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for the Believer that he humiliates himself.' I said, 'With what does he humiliate himself?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He undertakes what is beyond his capacity (from his resources).'

key_terms.يَتَعَذَّرُ: to be difficult or beyond capacity

ai.seo_question: How does a believer humiliate themselves according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises believers to avoid self-humiliation by not undertaking obligations they cannot fulfill, a principle rooted in the Shia concept of *tadarruj* (gradualism) and avoiding *ghabn* (loss of dignity). This teaching emphasizes practical wisdom in managing personal and financial commitments to preserve one's spiritual and social standing. It serves as a preventive measure against the shame of defaulting on promises or duties due to overextension.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not befitting for the Believer that he humiliates himself’. I said, ‘With what does he humiliate himself?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He indulges in what he cannot do from his (resources)’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘A believer must not humiliate himself.’ I then asked, ‘In what way can he humiliate himself?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘He can do so by involving himself in things that he cannot do.’”
